To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

five key factors are able to influence accountants' intention to adopt AIS: effort expectancy (β = 0.28, p < 0.01), perceived technology fit (β = 2.06, p < 1), facilitating conditions (β = 1.07, p < 5), self-efficacy (β = 5.06, p< 1) and coercive pressure (β = 3.05, p < 01).
five key factors (namely effort expectancy, perceived technological fit, facilitating conditions and coercive pressure) are able to influence accountants’ intention to adopt the AIS.
the five factors of effort expectancy, perceived fit of technology, facilitating conditions, perceived self-efficacy, and coercive pressure influence AIS adoption by accountans.

understanding the factors that influence the adoption of accounting information systems (e.g. enterprise resource planning, business intelligence and business analytics) by accountants.
the factors that influence AIS adoption by accountant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research is a useful addition to the literature in that it provides empirical evidence of factors affecting AIS adoption by accountancy professionals.
this research has successfully identified the factors that influence the adoption of AIS by accountants.
the adoption of AIS by accountants is influenced by effort expectancy, perceived fit of the AIS with their job, facilitating conditions, perceived self-efficacy to use the AIS and coercive pressure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adoption of AIS is not just a technical matter, but a complex social and political phenomenon.
this study provides a comprehensive model for understanding the factors that influence the adoption of AIS among accountants.
this study contributes to the AIS literature by providing a better understanding of the key factors influencing AIS adoption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adoption of AIS can be improved by increasing the perceived ease of use and the usefulness of AIS, and by providing sufficient resources and support for AIS adoption and use.
accounting professional bodies need to provide more training and technical support for accountants to enhance their self-efficacy in adopting the AIS.

accounting professionals are more likely to adopt the AIS if they perceive the AIS as easy to use, if they have sufficient technical knowledge, if they believe that the AIS would help them perform their jobs more efficiently, if the accounting professional body and the government encourage them to adopt it, and if they believe that their colleagues have adopted the AIS.
